A component record answers questions about one part. These rules answer the ones that span several — whether a divider built from two resistors keeps a third part inside its own limit, whether a clamp event stays under everything downstream of it. Each rule is projected whole from stored evidence: its conditions, the exact facts it rests on, any conditioned arithmetic, and the exact wording of what it refuses to conclude.

## How to read these rules

- **The refusal is the rule.** — Every rule states, in its own words, what may NOT be concluded from the evidence above it. That sentence is the rule's real output; the verdict is shorthand for it.
- **A verdict belongs to the rule, not to a part.** — A rule's verdict says how far the cross-component question has been settled. It is never a judgement about any of the parts the rule names, and the verdicts are never combined into one.
- **Calculations are conditioned, and the conditions are the point.** — Each calculation publishes its expression, its inputs and the exact results that were recorded, together with the conditions under which the answer means anything. A result read without them is arithmetic mistaken for a measurement.
- **Numbers here were carried, not computed.** — The expressions are published so a reader can redo the arithmetic. This page does not evaluate them — the results shown are the ones the evidence recorded.
- **An evidence chain does not flow downhill.** — A stage being settled says nothing about any stage after it. A document confirming a limit is not a measurement of the assembled board.

## rule-rail-envelope

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-rail-envelope" />

**What this rule asks:** Whether every part on the input rail stays inside its own recorded limits across a legal power contract, a mis-contract, and a transient clamp event.

- **Domain:** rail-envelope
- **Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not certify regulated output or the 26.5 W rated total until all three outputs pass low-line, full-load, ripple and thermal tests with the programmed PD core.

**Conditions:** Current chain: Board P nominal 15 V / 3 A -> AP63201 +13.44 V, LM2596 +6.519 V and -14.145 V intermediates -> LT1963A +12/+5 V and adjustable LT3015 -12.054 V nominal. R5/R6 are 10.5 k/1 k 0.1%; tolerance/TCR/reference calculations are screening, with actual low-line dropout, ripple and thermal coupling open. Board A and original regulator facts are historical and are not current-stage proof. Prototype normal source envelope is15 V±5%,20 V unsupported; first power/programming uses5 V-only with B disconnected and retained15 V-only NVM readback before a PD-capable source.

## rule-tvs-clamp-vs-absmax

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-tvs-clamp-vs-absmax" />

- **Domain:** tvs-clamp-vs-absmax
- **Verdict:** UNSOURCED

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not certify hot or installed surge survival from the25C table point or enable20V operation; measure source/gate/switch/rail transients and preserve downstream source-trust and attached-load limits.

**Conditions:** Current P D5 is Littelfuse SMAJ16A C74561 and B D3 is Diodes SDT5A60SA-13 C3024223. Normal prototype source input is 15 V ±5% (14.25..15.75 V), leaving only 0.25 V below 16 V standoff. The 26 V maximum clamp is specified at 15.4 A,10/1000 us,25C; it is not a universal hot/installed-surge ceiling, and VBR temperature coefficient cannot be applied as a VC correction. With selected full-temperature reference and 0.35% resistor/TCR negative maximum 14.814410 V, conditioned combined stress is40.814410 V: below U4 absolute45 V,D3 reverse60 V,C9 50 V, but above U4 operating40 V. STUSB28 V,Q1 VDS30 V and input capacitors35/50 V have conditioned margin. Output TVS/load limits and actual waveforms remain separate; old SMAJ20A32.4 V/SS34 40 V comparison is explicitly retired.

## rule-u4-inverting-stress

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-u4-inverting-stress" />

- **Domain:** u4-inverting-stress
- **Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not infer surge or startup acceptance from normal DC margin; preserve the negative rail, floating ground and semiconductor stress calculations after every setpoint change.

**Conditions:** U4 local GND/ON-OFF/tab ride the renewed negative intermediate. Normal prototype input is15 V±5%;20 V is unsupported. Effective input and D3 reverse stress are VBUS plus negative magnitude:29.145 V nominal,30.564410 V at15.75 V and the14.814410 V hot/TCR screen,40.814410 V at the conditioned26 V TVS point. New D3 has60 V reverse rating and maximum0.52 V at5 A/25C (0.45 V at5 A/125C); use0.52 V for the25C conduction screen, without extrapolating a full-temperature ceiling. C9 is50 V. CCM input-current/loss calculations include25C winding DCR, while hot DCR, switching/core/quiescent losses, ringing and startup remain open. Reverse leakage is0.5 mA maximum at60 V/25C and50 mA typical only at60 V/125C; the latter is not a guaranteed hot leakage bound. Reverse-leakage heating remains outside the forward-conduction model and requires qualification.

## rule-ldo-dropout-chain

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-ldo-dropout-chain" />

- **Domain:** ldo-dropout-chain
- **Verdict:** UNSOURCED

**This rule refuses to conclude:** The new parts improve DC headroom, but mirror-source trust, full-temperature adjustment bias on both regulator types, actual low-line ripple, capacitor stability and coupled thermal behavior remain open.

**Conditions:** LT1963A replaces both positive regulators and adjustable LT3015 replaces the negative regulator, programmed by R26+R27 = 8.88 k over R28 = 1 k to nominal -12.054 V. AP pre-rail arithmetic is 13.219794..13.6624 V with the selected resistor/TCR envelope. Negative minimum is 13.483572 V with full-temperature reference and 0.35% combined resistor tolerance/TCR, leaving 0.433472 V above the 13.0501 V worst-case output-plus-dropout requirement before ripple. The LT3015 ADJ bias limit is specified at 25C only. LT1963A adjustment-bias maximum is only specified at 25C; do not extrapolate it as a full-temperature limit. Include load-dependent ground current in thermal screens and verify output capacitor ESR/effective capacitance.

<EvidenceAnchor id="calc-renewal-negative-guarantee-margin" />

- **Expression:** `fact_lm2596_fb_vref_min_full_temp * (1 + fact_c861077_resistance * (1 - fact_c861077_tolerance / 100 - fact_c861077_tcr * temperature_delta_c / 1000000) / (fact_c110776_resistance * (1 + fact_c110776_tolerance / 100 + fact_c110776_tcr * temperature_delta_c / 1000000))) - input_requirement_v`

Both result rows use this single hot-case requirement, so the zero-excursion row is conservative rather than like-for-like.

## rule-q1-gate-drive-vs-contract

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-q1-gate-drive-vs-contract" />

- **Domain:** q1-gate-drive-vs-contract
- **Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not enable20 V or skip5 V-only first programming/readback; current gate arithmetic and a26 V table clamp do not qualify unknown factory NVM, hot surge response or measured gate/source behavior.

**Conditions:** Board P uses100 k source-to-gate/150 k gate-to-VBEN and source-referenced C35. Ideal asserted drive is-6 V at15 V,-6.3 V at15.75 V and-10.4 V at the26 V conditioned clamp point. These steady numbers do not establish transient gate safety. This prototype is15 V±5% only;20 V is unsupported and exceeds the new16 V TVS standoff. First power/programming must use a current-limited5 V-only source with B disconnected. Resolve jig voltage/pull-up loading and verify15 V-only NVM image/readback/reload before attaching any15 V-capable PD source. The archived-12.96 V result belongs to the retired32.4 V comparison.

### Source-to-bench evidence chain

The stages a claim passes through, in order. A settled stage says nothing about any stage after it: a manufacturer document confirming a limit is not an inspection of the assembled board, and neither is a measurement. A stage with no facts against it is not one nobody got round to filling in: nothing has been established there yet, so the rule's conditions and its refusal above are the whole of what is known about it.

## rule-screw-output-harness

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-screw-output-harness" />

- **Domain:** eurorack-output-harness
- **Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not preserve old same-net links between the two new poles: that would short distinct rails. Do not certify18A per output from a terminal rating or visual model; verify polarity, wire retention, process, hole fit and loaded temperature within shared board targets.

**Conditions:** J6.1 GND/J6.2 -12V and J7.1 +5V/J7.2 +12V are separate poles. Retaining an old same-node Faston link would deterministically short distinct rails, not create an acceptable bench assumption. Whole-board targets +12V/1.2A,+5V/0.5A,-12V/0.8A are shared with J10/J11. The2.5A sum-of-magnitudes return screen adds no capacity; no18A per-output board claim is established. Mirrored UL15A/300V and IEC18A/250V ratings are conditional terminal ratings. Actual wire, torque, solder process,1.30mm finished-hole fit, loaded temperature and retention remain unverified. Model tails3.50mm do not establish physical4.50±.20mm tail clearance; use4.70mm conservative geometry and retain physical qualification as open.

**Records this rule spans:**

- [`rec-c8465`](/docs/components/records/c8465/) — WJ500V-5.08-2P

## Raw agent resource

These rules are generated from a stored evidence bundle and do not restate it. The bundle is the source of truth: where the two ever disagree, the bundle is right and this page is stale.

No owning bundle is identified in the published model, so no reciprocal link can be given.
